items.front: Regulating Act 1773 — two firsts it created?
items.back: Office of Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings, 1st) and a Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774).
items.examPoint: Regulating Act 1773 — Governor-General of Bengal & Supreme Court at Calcutta
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Historical Background

items.front: Pitt's India Act 1784 — key institution and system it set up?
items.back: Board of Control for political affairs → 'double government' (Company + Crown).
items.examPoint: Pitt's India Act 1784 — Board of Control & double government
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Historical Background

items.front: Charter Act 1833 — office created and first holder?
items.back: Governor-General of India; Lord William Bentinck was the first. Ended the Company's commercial role.
items.examPoint: Charter Act 1833 — Governor-General of India (Bentinck) & legislative centralisation
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Historical Background

items.front: Charter Act 1853 — two landmark reforms?
items.back: Separated legislative & executive functions; introduced open competition for the ICS.
items.examPoint: Charter Act 1853 — legislative-executive separation & open competition for ICS
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Historical Background

items.front: Government of India Act 1858 — main changes?
items.back: Ended Company rule; Governor-General became Viceroy (1st: Canning); created Secretary of State for India.
items.examPoint: Government of India Act 1858 — end of Company rule, Viceroy & Secretary of State
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Historical Background

items.front: Indian Councils Act 1909 — popular name and hallmark?
items.back: Morley-Minto Reforms; introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
items.examPoint: Indian Councils Act 1909 — Morley-Minto Reforms & separate electorates
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Historical Background

items.front: GoI Act 1919 — popular name and key feature?
items.back: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms; introduced dyarchy in the provinces (transferred vs reserved subjects).
items.examPoint: Government of India Act 1919 — Montagu-Chelmsford & dyarchy in provinces
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Historical Background

items.front: GoI Act 1935 — why is it called the base of the Constitution?
items.back: Gave provincial autonomy, a Federal Court, RBI & PSCs; its structural framework became the Constitution's base.
items.examPoint: Government of India Act 1935 — provincial autonomy, Federal Court & structural base of the Constitution
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Historical Background

items.front: Indian Independence Act 1947 — main provisions?
items.back: Created two dominions (India, Pakistan) and made each Constituent Assembly sovereign. Based on Mountbatten Plan.
items.examPoint: Indian Independence Act 1947 — two dominions & Constituent Assemblies empowered
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Historical Background

items.front: Who first proposed a Constituent Assembly, and under which plan was it constituted?
items.back: M.N. Roy (1934); constituted in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan. 389 seats → 299 after partition; indirect election.
items.examPoint: Demand for a Constituent Assembly — M.N. Roy (1934), Nehru Report (1928), August Offer (1940)
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution

items.front: First Assembly meeting (9 Dec 1946): temporary vs permanent President?
items.back: Temporary: Sachchidananda Sinha; permanent (11 Dec 1946): Rajendra Prasad. B.N. Rau = constitutional advisor.
items.examPoint: First meeting (9 Dec 1946) & Sachchidananda Sinha as temporary/interim President
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution

items.front: Objectives Resolution — who moved it and when?
items.back: Moved by Nehru on 13 Dec 1946; passed 22 Jan 1947; became the basis of the Preamble.
items.examPoint: Objectives Resolution (Nehru, 13 Dec 1946; passed 22 Jan 1947)
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution

items.front: Drafting Committee — chair, size and date of formation?
items.back: Chaired by B.R. Ambedkar; 7 members; formed 29 August 1947.
items.examPoint: Drafting Committee — seven members under Ambedkar (established 29 Aug 1947)
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution

items.front: Duration, adoption/enforcement dates and original strength of the Constitution?
items.back: 2y 11m 18d; adopted 26 Nov 1949, in force 26 Jan 1950; 395 Articles, 22 Parts, 8 Schedules; handwritten by Prem Behari Narain Raizada.
items.examPoint: Adoption 26 Nov 1949 & enforcement 26 Jan 1950; handwritten by Prem Behari Narain Raizada
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution

items.front: Borrowed features: UK, USA, Ireland, Canada?
items.back: UK: parliamentary system; USA: Fundamental Rights + judicial review; Ireland: DPSP; Canada: federation with a strong Centre.
items.examPoint: Borrowed features & their sources (UK, US, Irish, Canadian and other constitutions)
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution

items.front: Under the Regulating Act 1773, what had the Court of Directors to report to the British Government?
items.back: Its revenue, civil and military affairs.
